podcast.body: A song from "Fully Completely" that tells the story of David Milgaard, who was wrongfully imprisoned. "Weekings, the story of the wrongfully imprisoned David Milgar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Identified as a deep track on *Fully Completely*, this song is noted for being "a really easy song to play." This characteristic makes it particularly popular for casual gatherings, described as a "great campfire" song and a "great summer thing for Canadians to do" due to the brevity of Canadian summers. "I think the song We Kings has touched a nerve for a lot of people. And I think maybe in part it's because it's a really easy song to play."

podcast.body: This song by The Tragically Hip is about the wrongful conviction of David Milgaard, a Manitoba man who was sentenced to life in prison on January 31, 1970, for the rape and murder of Gail Miller, a crime he did not commit. Milgaard served 21 years before his release and was later exonerated, with the true killer, Larry Fisher, eventually convicted. The members of The Tragically Hip met Milgaard several times in Winnipeg. "The tragically hip from fully completely with Wheat Kings inspired by the wrongful murder conviction of David Milgard."

podcast.body: This song is about David Milgard, a Manitoba man who was wrongfully convicted for the rape and murder of 20-year-old Saskatoon nursing assistant Gail Miller in 1970. Milgard, then 16, was sentenced to life in prison based on false testimony from two friends, and spent 21 years incarcerated before his release and subsequent exoneration two years later. An inquiry into the miscarriage of justice led to the conviction of Larry Fisher, the landlord of one of the false witnesses, for Gail Miller's murder in 2015. The members of The Tragically Hip met Milgard several times in Winnipeg. The song "38 Years Old" is explicitly stated not to be about Milgard. "Although he's never mentioned by name, the tragically hip song Wheat Kings is about David Milgard, a Manitoba man who was convicted for the rape and murder of a 20 year old Saskatoon nursing assistant named Gail Miller."
